idiom_name: generic Envelope<T> interface + JSON body envelope
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds the type-level half of the pattern: interface Envelope<T> { headers: Record<string, string>; payload: T } makes the wrapper explicit to the compiler, so wrap/unwrap helpers and guards are type-checked and the domain type T never has to know about transport metadata. The runtime is unchanged JSON - the classic envelope class is replaced by an object literal plus a type. Choose the CloudEvents variant when the event mesh standardizes attributes instead of a local schema.
pitfalls: `as Envelope<Order>` is an unchecked assertion: a malformed wire object passes silently, so validate at the seam before trusting headers or payload.
Generic JSON round-trips erase non-JSON payload types (Date, bigint, Buffer, undefined) - the envelope must own that conversion explicitly.
Header values are typed string here, but transports deliver string | string[] or Buffer; normalize during parsing or type the field honestly.

variants.name: CloudEvents SDK (standardized event envelope)
variants.implementation_notes: When the event mesh standardizes on CloudEvents, the envelope is the spec: the SDK's CloudEvent carries the required context attributes (id, source, type, specversion) plus a typed data payload, and the protocol binding decides where the envelope lives - HTTP.binary(ce) sends attributes as HTTP headers with the payload as body while HTTP.structured(ce) puts the whole event in the body; HTTP.toEvent({ headers, body }) unwraps at the destination. Choose it over a hand-rolled Envelope<T> when cross-producer/broker interoperability matters more than a minimal local schema.
pitfalls: Binary versus structured mode changes where the envelope lives; a receiver that only understands structured bodies silently loses the attributes of a binary-mode message.
Attribute names are constrained (lowercase alphanumeric, no 'data', 20 characters recommended) and extension attributes must not collide with core ones.
The SDK validates attribute types at construction; mutating the underlying plain object afterwards bypasses that validation.
